title: "Just one hour," I said. 4 hours later… 😴 한 시간만요 #learnkorean
caption:
한 시간만요 (han si-gan-man-yo) — "Just one hour, please."

You can say it at a Korean comic café (만화카페, man-hwa ka-pe): rent a tiny room with a blanket, read comics or nap, and pay by the hour.

When your time is up, the staff may ask:
연장하시겠어요? (yeon-jang-ha-si-ge-sseo-yo) — "Would you like to extend?"

To say no:
아니요, 괜찮아요. (a-ni-yo, gwaen-chan-a-yo) — "No, thank you."

Prices and rules differ by café — check the sign at the counter.

pinnedComment: Would you nap in a comic café? 😴 What’s your “just one hour” that turned into four? 👇
alt: A needle-felted Korean street: the coral felt mascot Mongle, exhausted, slumps in front of a cozy comic-book café. Text: When you need a nap in Korea… go to a 만화카페 (comic café) — rent a tiny room, pay by the hour. At the counter a felt staff doll asks 몇 시간 하실 거예요? (How many hours?) and Mongle says 한 시간만요! (Just one hour, please.). Mongle gets a tiny room with a mattress, blanket and comics, and melts into sleep. A wall clock's hands spin around three times: 3 hours later… The staff peeks through the curtain: 손님, 연장하시겠어요? (Your hour is up. Want more time?). Mongle half-opens its eyes: 아니요… 괜찮아요… (No, thank you.) — and falls right back asleep. The staff quietly closes the curtain, and the clock starts spinning again: “한 시간만요” — 4 hours and counting.
